# What Neon API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is. That run is sixteen characters, so a body is it four times over
# — the shortest body the pattern reads, since the count is a floor. It is
# spelled in lowercase where the case does not matter and in uppercase where the
# case is what a case is about: base62 holds the letters of both, so either
# spelling is a body.

patterns: neon-api-key

# The one prefix Neon has issued an API key with. There is a single kind of
# string here rather than a table of them: the personal key, the organization
# key and the project-scoped key are one format, so nothing in the value says
# which of them it is or what it reaches, and the cases below are that one shape
# in the places a key is written.

case:     a key in an environment assignment
in:       NEON_API_KEY=napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      NEON_API_KEY=«neon-api-key»

case:     a key in the bearer authorization header the Neon API is called with
in:       Authorization: Bearer napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      Authorization: Bearer «neon-api-key»

case:     a key in json
in:       {"key":"napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
out:      {"key":"«neon-api-key»"}

case:     a key on a command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" https://console.neon.tech/api/v2/projects
out:      curl -H "Authorization: Bearer «neon-api-key»" https://console.neon.tech/api/v2/projects

case:     a key in a configuration environment block
in:       "env": {"NEON_API_KEY": "napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
out:      "env": {"NEON_API_KEY": "«neon-api-key»"}

# The alphabet the sixty-four characters are written in. It is base62 — the
# letters of both cases and the digits. The two characters base64url adds, the
# hyphen and the underscore, are not admitted, and either of them ends a body.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       napi_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «neon-api-key»

case:     a body carrying a hyphen
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a body carrying an underscore
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a hyphen at the first character of the body, with a full run behind it
in:       napi_-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      napi_-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     an underscore at the first character of the body, with a full run behind it
in:       napi__0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      napi__0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The lengths either side of sixty-four. The count is read as a floor rather
# than exactly, so sixty-three characters are not a key and sixty-five are one
# key to the end of its run rather than a key and a character left over. What
# the floor costs is the middle case — a key cut short of sixty-four keeps every
# random character written in front of the cut, and none of them is redacted.

case:     a body of sixty-four characters is a key
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «neon-api-key»

case:     a body of sixty-three characters is not
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde
out:      napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcde

case:     an alphabet run longer than the floor is a key to the end of it
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0
out:      «neon-api-key»

# The three spellings Neon's own response examples write where a key goes. None
# of them is a prefix the library reads, so all three stay in the text, and the
# same body behind napi_ is redacted.

case:     the personal response example spelling
in:       neon_api_key_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      neon_api_key_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the organization response example spelling
in:       neon_org_key_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      neon_org_key_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the project-scoped response example spelling
in:       neon_project_key_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      neon_project_key_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The names Node-API writes with this prefix, which a source file of a native
# addon carries on nearly every line. None of them reaches a body: a name is
# snake_case, and the underscore after its next word ends the run long before
# the sixty-fourth character.

case:     a node-api call
in:       napi_create_string_utf8(env, name, NAPI_AUTO_LENGTH, &result);
out:      napi_create_string_utf8(env, name, NAPI_AUTO_LENGTH, &result);

case:     a node-api status
in:       napi_status status = napi_ok;
out:      napi_status status = napi_ok;

# What a key may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of the
# prefix, so a key keeps its span whatever word character it abuts — and where
# the run of its alphabet carries on past the floor, what carries it on is
# redacted with the key. A hyphen and an underscore end the run instead.
#
# A snake_case name whose segment closes on napi carries a whole prefix, so
# where sixty-four unbroken characters of the alphabet stand behind one,
# everything from the napi onward is redacted and only the syllable in front of
# it stays.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       NEON_API_KEY_napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      NEON_API_KEY_«neon-api-key»

case:     a key after a letter
in:       xnapi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      x«neon-api-key»

case:     a name closing on the prefix with a body behind it
in:       sonapi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      so«neon-api-key»

case:     a word written against a key
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefsuffix
out:      «neon-api-key»

case:     a hyphenated word written against a key
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef-suffix
out:      «neon-api-key»-suffix

case:     an underscored word written against a key
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef_suffix
out:      «neon-api-key»_suffix

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef.
out:      the key is «neon-api-key».

# Two keys written together. The four letters the prefix opens with belong to
# the alphabet a body is written in, so a body may close with napi and the
# underscore of the next key stand directly behind it; the second key begins
# four characters before the first one ends, the two spans overlap and are
# redacted as one. Written with nothing at all between them the first body
# reaches four characters into the second prefix and stops at the underscore
# behind them, so those two overlap as well. Written with a space between them
# the two are separate values, and both go.

case:     a key beginning inside the key before it
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abnapi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «neon-api-key»

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefnapi_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «neon-api-key»

case:     two keys separated by a space
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef napi_0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF0123456789ABCDEF
out:      «neon-api-key» «neon-api-key»

case:     a key followed immediately by japanese
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef日本語
out:      «neon-api-key»日本語

case:     a key preceded immediately by japanese
in:       日本語napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      日本語«neon-api-key»

case:     a key in a fragment of yaml
in:       NEON_API_KEY: napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      NEON_API_KEY: «neon-api-key»

case:     a key in a url query string
in:       https://console.neon.tech/api/v2/projects?key=napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef&p=1
out:      https://console.neon.tech/api/v2/projects?key=«neon-api-key»&p=1

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. The prefix closes with an
# underscore, which standard base64 writes nowhere, so only a base64url encoding
# can hold one — and where sixty-four base62 characters follow, the run from the
# prefix to the end of them is redacted whether or not Neon issued it. Such a
# run is a key's format exactly and nothing in the text tells the two apart, so
# sparing it would spare a real key written the same way.
#
# The digest is the same over-match taking a value a reader had a use for: a
# SHA-256 is sixty-four hexadecimal characters, which are base62 and carry
# nothing that ends a run. What holds either side of it is the floor and the
# prefix — a SHA-1 is forty characters, twenty-four short of a body, an MD5 is
# thirty-two, and a hyphen is no character the prefix carries.

case:     the prefix inside a longer run of base64url
in:       payload=zzzznapi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefzzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«neon-api-key»

case:     the prefix where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzznapi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdefzzzz
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«neon-api-key»

case:     a sha256 behind the prefix in a cache key
in:       key: napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      key: «neon-api-key»

case:     a sha1 behind the prefix, twenty-four characters short of a body
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an md5 behind the prefix
in:       napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha256 behind a hyphen rather than the prefix
in:       napi-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      napi-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# The prefix written in a case Neon does not issue keys in, the prefix without
# the underscore it closes with, and a body of the right length with no prefix
# at all.

case:     an uppercase prefix
in:       NAPI_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      NAPI_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the prefix with one letter capitalised
in:       Napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      Napi_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     the prefix without its closing underscore
in:       napi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      napi0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence
